edits.hebrew: מתני׳ בולשת שנכנסה לעיר בשעת שלום חביות פתוחות אסורות סתומות מותרות בשעת מלחמה אלו ואלו מותרות לפי שאין פנאי לנסך.
edits.english: MISHNA: In the case of a military unit [boleshet] that entered a city to stay there or collect taxes, if it entered during peacetime, then after the soldiers leave the open barrels of wine are forbidden, but the sealed barrels are permitted. If the unit entered in wartime, both these barrels and those barrels, even the open ones, are permitted, because in wartime there is no time for the soldiers to pour wine for idolatrous offerings, and one can be certain that the soldiers did not do so.

edits.hebrew: בולשת - חיל. על שם שמחפשין וחותרין, קרי להו בולשת, כדמתרגמינן: ויחפש ובלש.
edits.english: Boleshet - An army. They are called `boleshet` because they search and dig, as we translate [in Genesis 44:12]: 'and he searched and investigated'.

MISHNA: A boleshet (military unit) that entered a city to stay there or collect taxes, if it was during peacetime, open wine barrels are forbidden; if they were sealed, they are permitted. If it was in wartime, both these and those are permitted, even the open ones, because the soldiers have no time to pour libations.
